A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same RobustDLRT research. Their complete main texts, tables, figures, equations, and appendices are readable and support comparison despite reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original UCM and CIFAR10 experiments, including compression, adversarial accuracy, regularization sweeps, and black-box attacks.

after.justification: v2 retains original experiments and adds ImageNet evaluation, adversarial-training results, PGD experiments, and measured training runtimes.

M1.justification: The spectral regularizer, Algorithm 1's basis augmentation, coefficient updates and rank truncation, and the convolutional Tucker extension remain unchanged. Adversarial training is an additional experimental application of the retained method.

E1.justification: v2 adds actual ImageNet-1k training and evaluation, substantially extending coverage beyond UCM and CIFAR10 to 1,000-class image classification. In v1, ImageNet appears only as a source of pretrained weights.

E2.justification: The evaluated comparison methods remain full-rank training, DLRT, LoRA, Cayley SGD, Projected SGD, CondLR, and SVD pruning. The new PGD comparison reuses these methods; its additional CondLR settings are hyperparameter configurations. Newly cited pruning approaches are not added as evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: New protocols include ImageNet evaluation with ViT-32l and Top-1/Top-5 metrics, training batches containing 50% adversarial images, and randomly initialized iterative PGD attacks. For retained experiments, v1's Adam and ViT-32b with 32×32 patches become AdamW and ViT-16b with 16×16 patches in v2's specifications; unchanged scores do not establish reruns. The black-box table also changes its fourth attack-strength heading from 0.05 to 0.5.

E4.justification: v2 adds tests of robustness under iterative PGD attacks, compatibility with adversarial training, and measured regularization overhead. These address questions not experimentally tested in v1. The existing regularization-strength heatmaps and full-rank regularization analysis are retained.

E5.justification: The new adversarial-training Table 6 explicitly reports means over five repeated runs. Existing ten-run summaries, Table 2's standard deviations, Figure 2's five-run medians, and omission of error bars elsewhere remain unchanged; increased repetition of existing experiments is not established.

E6.justification: v2 adds ImageNet, adversarial-training, PGD, and runtime results. For example, Table 3 reports 57.98% compression and 25.24% Top-1 accuracy under FGSM at epsilon 0.3; Table 7 reports PGD accuracy of 16.59% versus the full-rank baseline's 29.93% at epsilon 0.3. Earlier numerical scores and heatmap entries are retained. These are additional results under new conditions, not demonstrated performance improvements between versions.

T1.justification: The regularizer definition, sensitivity and condition-number bounds, Propositions 1–3, and their appendix proofs remain mathematically unchanged. Renamed symbols and the added reminder defining Lipschitz continuity explain existing mathematics rather than introduce new assumptions or results.

C1.justification: The introduction reframes the contribution from a novel training framework to regularization incorporated into a class of existing low-rank frameworks. The conclusion changes 'over 94%' parameter reduction to 'up to 94%'. The central compression, accuracy, and robustness claims otherwise remain.

C2.justification: New Remark 3 acknowledges that raising small singular values could increase retained rank and reduce compression. v2 also discusses the cubic cost of full-rank regularization and qualifies PGD competitiveness by compression rate. Figure 3's explanation changes from modifying manifold curvature to steering training toward lower-curvature regions.

D1.justification: v2 supplies the ImageNet initialization checkpoint identifier, preprocessing instructions, ViT-32l hyperparameters, model parameter counts, and measured A100 runtimes. It also clarifies that experiments include biases. Existing hardware descriptions and attack-implementation access information are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds a paragraph positioning the method against sparsity pruning, with several pruning-and-robustness references, plus references supporting adversarial training and PGD. Existing low-rank and orthogonality positioning remains. The retained FGSM comparison's source attribution is corrected to the CondLR paper.

P1.justification: v2 places the initial spectral discussion before related work and gives regularization its own section. Appendices are reorganized into additional results, experimental details, and proofs. Most existing prose is retained, alongside local wording, notation, and conference-header edits.

P2.justification: The empirical displays expand substantially through dedicated ImageNet, adversarial-training, and PGD tables, plus expanded hyperparameter tables. Table 2 highlights baseline-surpassing results, Figure 1 is restyled, and Figure 2 gains explicit panel labels. Existing appendix heatmaps are retained, with the duplicate Mixup figure caption removed.

improvement.justification: ImageNet evaluation and the new adversarial-training and PGD tests strengthen evidence for scalability, compatibility, and robustness limits beyond v1's experiments. Added qualifications also improve interpretation. However, incomplete PGD settings and unexplained optimizer/ViT specification changes limit reproducibility. The new runtime claim is inconsistent: 26m 07s versus 27m 51s implies approximately 6.6% overhead, not the stated 3%. These reporting issues limit the overall gain.
